heading_en: Reduction and Addition of Inter-character Spacing
heading_ja: 文字クラスに応じた空き量の変更

cases.quote: Line adjustment by hanging punctuation is a method of avoiding line head wrap of full stops (cl-06) and commas (cl-07). This method is not formally defined in JIS X 4051, however JIS X 4051 does provide explanatory material about it.
cases.rationale: §3.8.2 lists hanging punctuation as one of the methods available once reduction has run, and `Question::HANGING_PUNCTUATION` (JLReq §3.8.2 itself, `spec/derived/questions.tsv` row `adjustment.hanging_punctuation`) is the switch: `Policy::JLREQ` selects `none`, JLReq's own stated default, and `hanging` is the named alternative. The fixture is deliberately the smallest one that tells the two apart: one ideograph (亜) and one full stop (。) whose own trailing half-em space (§B.2 note 6) is the line's entire flexibility. At `measure = 1300` the natural extent is 2000 (1000 for 亜, 500 for 。, 500 for the trailing half-em), 700 over measure; the trailing space is `Reduction::Discrete { floor: 0, stage: 2 }` (Table 3's `before: 6, after: line-edge` cell), so `reduce` closes 500 of the 700 by flipping it to solid, leaving 200 still owed. Under the default policy nothing else in this two-item line can absorb that 200 — there is no earlier candidate this fixture offers, so the line the greedy search commits to is reported `Overfull(200)` (`RuleId::POSSIBILITIES_FOR_LINE_BREAKING_BETWEEN_CHARACTERS`, address `C`, the address every `ViolationKind` in this crate cites) rather than silently accepted. In a paragraph with more text after it, the only way to close that same 200 units without hanging would be to pull the full stop down onto the next line's own head — which §3.1.7/Table 2 already forbid (cl-06 may never start a line), so the realistic alternative is reducing something earlier in the paragraph instead, at the cost of a visibly different break. Hanging punctuation exists precisely to avoid needing either: under `adjustment.hanging_punctuation = hanging`, `ladder::hang` lets 。sit past the measure for exactly the 200 units reduction could not place (`shortfall.min(item.advance())`, and the full stop's own 500-unit advance comfortably covers it), the line is reported conforming, and `Line::hanging()` names the full stop and the 200-unit overhang. `Line::extent()` excludes that overhang by `docs/adr/0017`'s own definition, which is why the two entries below agree on `placements` (the hung character's own box does not move, only the measure it is judged against changes) but disagree on `extent`, `hanging` and `violations`. Only the default entry (`adjustment.hanging_punctuation = none`) is exercised by a run of this suite: `Kumihan::default()` declares `Policy::JLREQ`, which selects `none`, so the `hanging` entry is never the applicable one `jlreq_conform::run` measures the workspace against. It is published for an implementation that declares that alternative, and its own arithmetic is verified separately, by `crates/jlreq-line/src/compose.rs`'s own `a_hung_characters_overhang_is_excluded_from_the_lines_own_extent` unit test — the identical fixture, already green — rather than by this file.

forbidden.why: §2.5.1's own definition credits hanging punctuation with keeping the measure aligned, not with adding to it on top of what reduction already gave up: `docs/adr/0017-normalized-line-geometry.md` excludes the hung amount from `Line::extent()` precisely so a hung line still reads as reaching the measure it was composed against. Reporting `extent: 1500` (reduction's own result) alongside a nonzero `hanging` answers a line that was both left overfull and credited with hanging for the same shortfall, which is not a reading either entry above states — `hanging` only ever accompanies `extent: 1300`, the fully-closed measure.
